resources.when: from 4:00, then every lesson from now on

resources.detail: paper and pencil work fine at home
trace the sound and the words

flow.does: Welcome, then the sound talk game. My turn: s-u-n. Your turn: children blend it back as sun. Repeat with s-a-t and s-i-p. Voices only; nothing written. Pause-point after each my turn.
flow.point: Blending by ear comes before blending in print. No cards to speed-review yet; from Lesson 2 every lesson opens with the speed review.

flow.does: Introduce the sound with my turn, your turn: /sss/. Show the mouth position: teeth close together, air hissing out. Stretch it like a snake: sssss. Every child says it alone at least once.
flow.point: Pure sound, always: /sss/, never 'suh'. No added vowel on the end.

flow.step: See it: Sound Book and sound card
flow.does: Open Sound Book 's' and enjoy the sun photos: say /sss/ each time the letter appears. Then sound card 's': say it together, then cold. Pause-point: card up, wait, reveal.
flow.point: The letter is the picture of the sound. We say the sound, not the letter name; if a child offers 'ess', celebrate and anchor: today we say /sss/.

flow.does: Model the patter twice, slowly: start at the top, curve round the snake's head, then swing back the other way. Sky-write three times together, then whiteboards: the two-minute write-it moment. Check every board.
flow.point: Start at the top, every time. The curve is often reversed, so watch the first stroke, not the finished shape.

flow.does: Say a string of sounds and words (m, sss, sun, dog, sock); children signal every time they hear /sss/. One teaser blend to finish: s-a-t. Tomorrow we blend. Close with the home note in the footer.
flow.point: Every child proves the sound alone today; anyone unsure gets the keep-up eye tomorrow.

language.label: /s/ as in sun · the first sound of the whole journey
language.words_label: Unlocking this week and next (do not show in print today)
language.note: Week one has no code to blend with yet: today is oral blending and formation only. These words unlock within days, once a, t and p arrive. Tricky words I and the are met later this week.

watch_for: A continuous, hissy sound: hold it /sss/, never 'suh'. No added vowel.
Formation: the snake curve is often reversed. Watch the first stroke; insist on starting at the top.
Letter-name interference: children who know the alphabet song will offer 'ess'. Anchor the sound instead.
Pencil grip and whiteboard posture: model both before the write-it moment.
1.home: Today's sound is /sss/. Hunt for five /sss/ things and sky-write s three times. The first reading (Tap! Tap! Tap!) goes home after Day 5; daily practice continues in the parent app, matched to this lesson.
